_meta.status: batch 1 -- first 10 states, more to follow in a later batch
_meta.purpose: Per-state CPA license reinstatement cost + penalty-CPE data: what a lapsed CPA actually owes to get reinstated (fee + catch-up CPE hours + ethics hours), sourced fresh -- this dataset did not exist anywhere on the site before 2026-07-25. Same 2-source verification standard as cpa_deadlines.json and cpe_hours.json: a board page + a codified rule/statute for every record. Genuinely empty shelf per ScoutLab's 2026-07-21 product register (no per-state reinstatement calculator exists anywhere) -- built as the free lead-magnet the affiliate-only monetization pivot recommended, not a paid SKU.
_meta.publish_rule: 2-source standard: board page + codified rule/statute for every record. A state whose real-world fee/hours figure is a formula (not a flat number) reports null in the numeric field and explains the formula in the matching *_notes field and data_gap_note -- never a guessed point figure.
_meta.does_not_touch: cpa_deadlines.json / cpe_hours.json unchanged -- this is a new, independent dataset.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Codified reinstatement fee is $500 (S.C. Code Ann. § 40-2-250(F)), paid in addition to the standard $95 annual renewal fee the board lists on its FAQ -- $595 total out-of-pocket.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 CPE hours for EACH year the license was lapsed (cumulative catch-up). If lapsed 3+ years, the requirement jumps to 120 hours (completed within the preceding 3 years) plus 6 months of additional qualifying experience.
records.lapse_trigger: Not renewed by February 1; considered lapsed if not renewed by February 15 at 11:59pm.
records.citation: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-2-250 (Renewal of licenses; reinstatement of lapsed licenses), subsections (E)-(G); definitions in § 40-2-20

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reissuance-of-forfeited-certificate application fee (21 NCAC 08J .0106(b)(1)), 'plus penalties' per the Board's own fee schedule -- no primary-law source ties a specific extra dollar figure to routine late-renewal forfeiture, so treat as a floor, not a hard ceiling.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 CPE hours completed in the 12 months immediately preceding the reinstatement application (21 NCAC 08J .0106(b)(3)) -- the same total as one year's ordinary renewal, not extra hours. NC does not require make-up CPE for years spent forfeited.
records.lapse_trigger: License is FORFEITED if not renewed by July 1, the Board mails a demand letter, and renewal (application + CPE + fee) still isn't completed within 30 days of that letter's mailing date.
records.citation: 21 NCAC 08J .0106 (Forfeiture of Certificate and Reissuance), with 21 NCAC 08J .0101/.0105(c), 21 NCAC 08F .0504, and N.C. Gen. Stat. § 93-12(15)/(7a)/(9)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: K.A.R. 74-12-1(e): $247.50 if more than one year remains in the current biennial period at application time, or $123.75 if one year or less remains.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 hours of qualifying CE completed within the 12 months preceding the reinstatement application (K.S.A. 1-310(g)) -- half the normal 80-hour/2-year total, but concentrated into one year. These hours cannot also be counted toward the next renewal (K.A.R. 74-4-10).
records.lapse_trigger: Permit expires biennially on the next July 1 after issuance/renewal. Late renewal is possible within 12 months of expiration; beyond 12 months, formal reinstatement (not simple late renewal) is required.
records.citation: K.S.A. 1-310(g) (reinstatement trigger, 40-hour CPE requirement); K.A.R. 74-12-1(e) (fee schedule); K.A.R. 74-4-10 (2-hour ethics component)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Double the standard $63 renewal fee (COMAR 09.24.01.09.B(9)/(4)). Charged as soon as the license's 2-year expiration date passes; the Board's FAQ states it currently cannot be waived.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Same standard 80-hour/2-year total as ordinary renewal, not an extra amount -- the catch is timing: those 80 hours must be earned within 2 years of the reinstatement application date (COMAR 09.24.02.05.A) and can't also be counted toward the next renewal cycle.
records.lapse_trigger: Not renewed by the license's fixed 2-year expiration date. No statutory outer time limit was found after which reinstatement becomes unavailable.
records.citation: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 2-314 (Reinstatement); COMAR 09.24.01.09.B (fees); COMAR 09.24.02.03 (80-hr/4-ethics-hr CE requirement); COMAR 09.24.02.05.A (2-year CE lookback)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reinstatement-of-a-null-and-void-license application fee (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-31.015). Reinstatement from null-and-void is discretionary (board must find good-faith effort defeated by illness/hardship, s. 473.313(5), Fla. Stat.) -- not a routine online renewal. A separate $25 delinquent-status fee may also apply but could not be independently confirmed against a codified rule.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Two-step climb of 120 hours each (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-33.006): 120 hrs to move null-and-void back to delinquent, then another 120 hrs to move delinquent back to active. 160 hours above Florida's normal 80-hour biennial requirement; all must fall within the 24 months preceding the application.
records.lapse_trigger: License goes DELINQUENT on January 1 following failure to report CPE for biennial renewal; if not cured, remains delinquent for 2 years and then AUTOMATICALLY becomes NULL AND VOID (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-30.030), no further board action required.
records.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-31.015 ($250 reinstatement fee); r. 61H1-30.030 (2-year automatic null-and-void trigger); r. 61H1-33.006 (120+120-hr CPE, 8 ethics hrs/step); s. 473.313(5), Fla. Stat. (discretionary reinstatement)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No flat fee -- a tiered multiplier of the base renewal fee under 22 TAC § 515.5: 1.5x if expired ≤ 90 days, 2x if expired 90 days–1 year, 3x if expired 1–2 years; at 2+ years (revocation-eligible) the licensee owes all accrued renewal + late fees for the lapsed period, not a simple multiple. At the current $118/yr base individual fee this computes to roughly $177 / $236 / $354 for the first three tiers.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 22 TAC § 523.112 requires a former licensee reinstating after revocation to 'report the minimum CPE credits missed' rather than a fixed extra/penalty hour count -- no flat figure exists in the rule text.
records.lapse_trigger: Individual licenses renew annually by the last day of the licensee's birth month. Missing that deadline triggers the escalating late-fee tiers above. Failure to complete renewal for 3 consecutive years lets the Board revoke the license under Tex. Occ. Code § 901.502(4); reinstatement after revocation requires Board action, not a simple late renewal.
records.citation: 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 515.5 (Late Filing for Renewal of License); Tex. Occ. Code § 901.502(4); 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 523.112 (Required CPE Participation)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Statutory cap, not a flat fee: $50 restoration fee plus all lapsed annual renewal fees ($40/yr Licensed CPA, $30/yr Registered CPA), capped so the total 'shall not exceed $260' (68 Ill. Admin. Code 1420.40). Restoring from voluntary inactive status costs only the current renewal fee instead.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the normal 120-hour/3-year total (68 Ill. Admin. Code 1420.60/1420.70) -- restoration just requires those 120 hours to fall within the 3 years immediately preceding the restoration application, not an additional amount.
records.lapse_trigger: Individual license expires September 30 every 3 years (firm license: November 30) if not renewed in the 2-month pre-expiration window. No grace period -- practicing on an expired license is unlicensed activity from the day after expiration (68 Ill. Admin. Code 1420.80).
records.data_gap_note: penalty_cpe_hours/penalty_ethics_hours are null because the rule imposes the same standard 120-hr/4-ethics-hr load already required at ordinary renewal, just with a tighter lookback window -- not an additional number. IDFPR's own site does not publish CPA-specific restoration dollar figures on a single page (its general reactivation-fee table explicitly excludes CPAs); the board-page leg of the 2-source rule is satisfied by the Public Accounting landing page instead, with the exact fee formula confirmed only in the codified rule text.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reinstatement-of-inactive-or-expired-license fee, paid IN ADDITION TO the current $100 biennial renewal fee -- $135 total plus any CPE course costs.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Same standard 80-hour total as ordinary biennial renewal (49 Pa. Code § 11.62(c)), not an extra amount -- the only difference is the 80 hours must fall within the 24 months immediately preceding the reactivation filing, rather than the fixed biennial period.
records.lapse_trigger: Not renewed by 11:59pm December 31 of odd-numbered years. The Board states explicitly there is no grace period; the license lapses effective January 1 and a reactivation application (not a standard renewal) is required.
records.citation: 49 Pa. Code § 11.4 (fees, $35 reinstatement); § 11.62(c) (reactivation CPE, 80 hrs/24-month lookback); § 11.63(a)(7) (4-hour ethics minimum)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No flat fee -- a monthly late-filing charge under ORC 4701.10(D)-(E): up to $100/month (cap $1,200) for a practicing permit holder, up to $50/month (cap $300) for a registration/non-practicing holder. If the Board finds 'excusable neglect' (ORC 4701.10(F)), it may instead set a reduced fee (not exceeding $50 plus the standard triennial permit fee per lapsed period).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Same 120-credit/3-year total as ordinary renewal (Ohio Admin. Code 4701-15-02(A)), but reinstatement (OAC 4701-15-09) requires all 120 within the 36 months immediately preceding the application AND subject-matter minimums ordinary renewal doesn't impose: at least 24 credits in accounting/auditing/assurance/attestation, at least 24 in taxation.
records.lapse_trigger: Permits/registrations expire December 31 on a staggered triennial cohort cycle (not one date for all licensees). Failing to renew within ONE YEAR of that expiration date suspends the underlying CPA certificate/PA registration (ORC 4701.10(F)) until accrued late fees are paid or a reduced fee is approved.
records.citation: Ohio Rev. Code § 4701.10(A),(B),(D),(E),(F); Ohio Admin. Code 4701-15-02(D), 4701-15-09 (120 credits/36 months, 24 A&A, 24 tax, 3 ethics)
records.data_gap_note: reinstatement_fee_usd is null because Ohio's own law sets a formula/cap, not a flat number (reported in the notes field instead). The Board's own fees page could not be directly fetched during research (repeated 404, independently reproduced) -- its figures are corroborated via multiple independent search-engine text extractions that match the statute text verbatim-fetched from codes.ohio.gov, but this is a real gap on the board-page leg of the 2-source rule until a live-render check succeeds. Recommend a manual browser spot-check before this record is cited anywhere beyond this page.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Non-refundable reinstatement fee (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 20-10-.04(1)(a)), payable in addition to completing the CPE catch-up requirement.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 hours of CPE for each year since the license last renewed, capped at 160 hours (double the normal 80-hour/2-year renewal). At least 20% of the total must be in accounting/auditing subjects, and at least 80 hours must fall within the 2 years immediately preceding the application; no carryover allowed.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire December 31 of odd-numbered years. A 4-month penalty period follows, during which the license can still be renewed by paying a $100 penalty fee plus the renewal fee. After that window closes, reinstatement (not renewal) is required.
records.citation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 20-10-.04 (Reinstatement); r. 20-10-.02 (Biennial Renewal); r. 20-10-.03 (Penalty Period/Late Renewal)
